lines.text: Yes, this world becomes God's garden, its apparent reality
becomes genuine reality as a result of the fact that we are
invited to encounter therein the love of God and are privi-
leged to impart that love to others. And if our joy this
Christmastide is to be and must be that we receive anew the
gift of divine love and are freed by it to love with new power
and inspiration, is not that something which will unite us
with those who are fighting for us? They too are offered the
gift of this joy and upon them too has this light shined, and
all of us, both those at home and those out there at the front,
must help each other to prepare ourselves to receive this joy
and this light. At Advent we should make it clear to our-
selves that we are faced here by an issue which calls for vital
decision. Do we or do we not desire these divine gifts? Do
we truly want the heavenly light to shine in our earthly
darkness? Are we prepared to admit that our world, and
that we ourselves, are wrapped in thick darkness? Let us
rightly understand this summons to decision, let us obey the
call to discipleship! Which of us can tell how much longer
he will have to hear the Word?
"The light is with you for a little longer. Walk while you
have the light, lest the darkness overtake you; he who walks
in the darkness does not know where he goes. While you
have the light, believe in the light, that you may become
sons of light."
